transfer.questionContent: {"id":"aortic-image-quality-contrast","version":1,"prompt":"A different fictional patient has sudden severe chest pain. The CTA report says motion obscures the ascending aorta and calls that segment nondiagnostic. No definite flap is reported. Which conclusion best respects this evidence?","choices":[{"id":"excluded","label":"The absence of a reported flap excludes an aortic process.","feedback":"A nondiagnostic segment is not a reliable negative finding. The report explicitly limits what can be concluded."},{"id":"unresolved","label":"The aortic question remains unresolved; the team needs to clarify the inadequate study.","feedback":"The limitation matters. Image acquisition and motion affect diagnostic confidence, so an inadequate segment cannot carry an exclusion claim."},{"id":"confirmed","label":"The symptom pattern alone confirms dissection despite the report.","feedback":"The symptoms justify concern, not certainty. The fictional report has not established the diagnosis."}],"answerId":"unresolved","source":{"title":"2022 ACC/AHA Aortic Disease Guideline: CT image quality","url":"https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/10.1161/CIR.0000000000001106"},"synthetic":true,"reviewStatus":"pending_human_review","sourceCheckedDate":"2026-09-11"}
